categories.summary: Saudi air defences destroyed a Houthi cruise missile over Riyadh on 28 November with no damage reported (confirmed by the Saudi-led coalition), after Wednesday's deadly hit on the Jazan refinery. Saudi Arabia and the Houthis are now trading strikes aimed at each other's capitals. Iran's Revolutionary Guards again claim ships hit mines in Hormuz; maritime press also reports a gas carrier hit with a seafarer missing, not yet independently confirmed. No newly confirmed attacks on US bases since Kuwait's 26 November drone strike. Taiwan and Korea are quiet.

categories.name: Nuclear & fallout
categories.summary: US nuclear-command aircraft are normal. Forecast markets give a Russian or US nuclear test this year only about 2-3%.

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure
categories.summary: Flight Centre is still investigating the theft of customer details, including passports, from an outside booking system; who did it is not known. The suspected China campaign (partly blamed on China by governments) touches Australia; the FBI warns criminals and state hackers are using an AI tool called ARTEX to automate attacks, and South Korea has launched an emergency response to AI-driven hacking. Korea Post reports a hack of its mobile service (about 113,000 customers). Australian phones, banks and the grid look normal, but our phone-network and internet monitors are timing out.

drivers: Flight Centre, an Australian company, says hackers took customer details including passports from an outside booking system. Who did it is not known; it may be criminals, not a state.

If the China-linked hacking is one deliberate campaign, the likely aim is quiet footholds in allies' phone, power and water networks ahead of any Taiwan crisis, with phone networks, utilities and ports the likely next targets. This is a hypothesis, though governments have blamed China for parts of it.

A run of big overseas hacks continues (EU Commission, US intelligence systems, FBI database), and Switzerland says AI agents were used in five attacks including on utilities. Suspected Iran-linked attacks on shop freezers and small water systems remain overseas.

headline: Saudi Arabia shot down another Houthi missile over Riyadh today with no damage reported; fuel in SA is steady and the Hills fire danger drops to Moderate tomorrow.
summary: Saudi air defences destroyed a Houthi cruise missile over Riyadh on Saturday, confirmed by the Saudi-led coalition, with no damage reported; it did not hit any oil site. We checked for new attacks on US bases, tankers and Gulf cities and oil sites in the last day and found no newly confirmed hits beyond this; Iran again claims ships hit mines in Hormuz, which is not independently confirmed. Oil is near US$91 and SA fuel is steady with no shortages. Fire danger in the Hills is High today and Moderate tomorrow; there are no warnings near home.
